properties.areaDesc: Maricopa, AZ; Pinal, AZ
properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 20 at 9:49PM MST until October 20 at 10:30PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
SVRPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1030 PM MST.

* At 949 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 6 miles southwest
of Chandler Fashion Center Mall, or 6 miles west of Sun Lakes,
moving northeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is possible. Wind damage to roofs,
siding, and trees possible.

* Locations impacted include...
Phoenix, Mesa, Chandler, Scottsdale, Gilbert, Tempe, Paradise
Valley, Sun Lakes, East Mesa, Fiesta Mall, Mesa Riverview Mall,
Tempe Marketplace, Downtown Mesa, Arizona State University, Salt
River Indian Community, Papago Park, Arizona Mills Mall, Downtown
Scottsdale, Chandler Fashion Center Mall and Chandler City Hall.

This includes the following highways...
AZ Route 87 between mile markers 161 and 170. AZ Route 202 between
mile markers 10 and 19. AZ Route 101 between mile markers 39 and 48.
US Highway 60 between mile markers 173 and 182. AZ Interstate 10
between mile markers 151 and 160. AZ Route 347 between mile markers
185 and 189.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

Report severe weather to your nearest law enforcement agency or the
National Weather Service office in Phoenix AZ.

properties.areaDesc: Castle Country; San Rafael Swell
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 10:11PM MDT until October 23 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country and San Rafael Swell.

* WHEN...From Wednesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A late season surge of tropical moisture will bring widespread
moderate to at times heavy rainfall across much of eastern Utah
beginning Wednesday afternoon, and continuing through Thursday.
Local rainfall totals in excess of 2 inches are expected through
Thursday evening.
- All normally dry washes, small streams and mainstem rivers will
see elevated flows from this excessive rainfall, with periods of
heavier rainfall resulting in flash flooding. Backcountry roads
may become impassable due to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

People in the backcountry should ensure they have alternative routes
available in case their primary route becomes impassable.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH THURSDAY EVENING

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 20 at 8:35PM PDT until October 22 at 11:00AM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...There is an 80% chance of 4 inches or more of snow along the
Tioga Pass and highway 120. There is a 50-60% chance for four
inches or more of snow above 8,000 feet in Tulare, Madera, and
Fresno Counties.

* WHERE...Above 8,000 feet in the Sierra Nevada.

* WHEN...From 11 AM Wednesday to 11 AM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely
become slick and hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snowfall will affect traffic across Tioga
Highway/Pass.
properties.instruction:
Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

properties.areaDesc: West Side Mountains South of 198; Buttonwillow - Lost Hills - I5; Buena Vista; Bakersfield; South End San Joaquin Valley; Kern River Valley; Piute Walker Basin; Tehachapi; Grapevine; Frazier Mountain Communities; Indian Wells Valley; Mojave Desert Slopes; Mojave Desert
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 20 at 8:34PM PDT until October 22 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall from storms
training over the same area.

* WHERE...A portion of central California, including the following
areas, Bakersfield, Buena Vista, Buttonwillow - Lost Hills - I5,
Frazier Mountain Communities, Grapevine, Indian Wells Valley, Kern
River Valley, Mojave Desert, Mojave Desert Slopes, Piute Walker
Basin, South End San Joaquin Valley, Tehachapi and West Side
Mountains South of 198.

* WHEN...From 8 AM PDT Wednesday through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become
clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Strong area of low pressure off the Southern California coast
will move inland and interact with tropical moisture.
- Be especially careful on Highway 58 between mile markers 101 to
103 and the Borel burn scar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
